shortName: Michigan State University College of Human Medicine

medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: A medical student may need to take a voluntary leave of absence for a variety of reasons (personal, financial, medical, etc.).  A leave of absence will be granted for an initial maximum of one year. Students may petition for an extension. Any student on leave for more than two calendar years will be required to comply with readmission criteria established by Michigan State University. There is an eight-year time limit on the entire medical student program, which includes leaves of absence.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: The MSU College of Human Medicine, along with student groups, coordinates several volunteer clinical programs to help students sharpen their clinical skills and have the opportunity to serve the communities in which they will live. Students participate in a wide variety of student organizations for professional development, personal growth, service, and fun.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: Students spend years one and two at the MSU Big Ten campus in East Lansing or the campus in the health sciences corridor in downtown Grand Rapids. Students experience years three and four at one of eight clinical community campuses located throughout the state. Community campuses are located in urban, suburban, and rural areas.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Affordable housing is readily available off-campus at all sites.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: The College supports students who identify as a gender and/or sexual minority with student organizations and student wellness faculty, who assist students with navigating career and life challenges if needed.  Faculty and staff are directed to and encouraged to engage programming that is pertinent to self-improvement, education, and cultural sensitivity as it pertains to gender and sexual minorities.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: Students on the East Lansing campus have access to all student recreation facilities.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: The MSU College of Human Medicine (CHM) offers students a positive and supportive learning environment to promote their personal and professional growth and well-being throughout their medical education. The Shared Discovery Curriculum emphasizes collaborative and team-based learning, prompting students to develop meaningful longitudinal relationships with peers and faculty mentors as they gain the knowledge and skills required to become competent and compassionate physicians. With service at the core of our mission, students at CHM are actively engaged in opportunities that positively impact the physical and social well-being of community members across the state.

medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: The College of Human Medicine offers tutoring through Academic Achievement. Students can request tutors throughout their medical school education.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Emphasis on small group and highly structured self-directed learning.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Timely attendance at all scheduled activities is expected, absences should be rare.  Records are kept and are a part of the end-of-semester competence committee assessment.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
Michigan State University and the College of Human Medicine have longstanding histories of pedagogical innovation and success. The delivery of medical care is undergoing change, and physicians need new kinds of knowledge and skills to provide excellent care. In response to this, we have designed and developed a new approach to adult learning in medical school that we call the Shared Discovery Curriculum (SDC).  

The SDC is an integrated curriculum that integrates underlying necessary basic and disease sciences along with clinical experience throughout all four years of the educational program - progressively building upon previously learned material. Students learn the clinical skills and necessary science they need to take care of patients throughout the entire curriculum. The curriculum emphasizes learning by doing and being useful in real clinical settings.

Students and faculty work and learn together in partnership to build strong relationships.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: Michigan State University College of Human Medicine is nationally recognized as a community-based medical education institution built upon the core value of serving the people. Founded in 1964 to respond to Michigan's need for primary care physicians, we pride ourselves on providing exceptional medical education to a diverse group of students by harnessing the powers of innovation, engaging in excellent medical service and discovery that advance health, encouraging ethical and social responsibility, and providing a collegial and collaborative learning environment.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms:
As a community-based medical school, one goal of CHM is to conduct collaborative, multidisciplinary and multi-community research that takes advantage of our unique distributed campus system. Our focus is on both clinical research that can be practically applied as well as the critical research in the basic science departments affiliated with CHM (Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, Microbiology and Molecular Genetics, Pharmacology, and Physiology) on mechanisms underlying human diseases, and their integration.

Our Mission: To promote and support health and biomedical research, infrastructure, and culture within the CHM campus system and collaborative research across disciplines, departments, colleges, campuses, and communities.

Our Philosophy: Research is an important and integral component of CHM. It informs and transforms our teaching and clinical environment into one where knowledge is used and disseminated but also actually produced. It keeps us on the leading edge of medicine.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: The College of Human Medicine has a presence in over 50 inpatient institutions in eight communities.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: The College of Human Medicine (CHM), founded in response to Michigan's need for primary care physicians, has expanded in mission and size to meet growing needs. Students begin at either the MSU campus in East Lansing or at the Grand Rapids campus. After the first two years of early and middle clinical experience within the Shared Discovery Curriculum, students complete their late clinical experience at one of eight community campuses.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: The College of Human Medicine at Michigan State University is committed to educating exemplary physicians and scholars, discovering and disseminating new knowledge, and providing service at home and abroad. We enhance our communities by providing outstanding primary and specialty care, promoting the dignity and inclusion of all people, and responding to the needs of the medically underserved.

medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: Letters of evaluation should be written by individuals who know you well and can objectively assess your academic readiness for medical school, personal characteristics, and/or ability to engage with others in academic, clinical, or community-based settings. While not required, applicants are encouraged to obtain a letter from a supervisor in a clinical setting. Letters from family members and/or friends are discouraged.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: Interviews will be held virtually for the 2026-2027 academic year. Detailed information is communicated electronically to those offered an interview.
medSchoolApplication.interviewInvitations: Invitations begin in August.  Interviews are conducted from September through February.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: A multiple mini-interview and 30-minute traditional one-on-one interview with a current medical student. All interviews are virtual.
medSchoolApplication.secApplSentTo: Applicants who meet minimum academic criteria: BCPM GPA of 2.5 or above and MCAT score of 498 and above.
medSchoolApplication.acceptOutstateApplInformation: While preference is given to in-state applicants, out-of-state applicants with ties to the state of Michigan and/or a sincere interest in serving underserved communities are encouraged to apply.
medSchoolApplication.acceptCanadianApplInformation: Must be Canadian citizen. Non-Canadian citizenship with permanent resident visa in Canada does not qualify.
medSchoolApplication.acceptInternationalApplInformation: Canadian citizens are considered out-of-state applicants.
medSchoolApplication.dacaDetail: Preference given to DACA in-state residents.
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo: MSU College of Human Medicine uses a mission-aligned selection process to identify candidates for our MD program. We admit individuals who demonstrate academic excellence; commitment to service and community; personal characteristics and competencies consistent with the profession of medicine; and potential to advance the mission of our college.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: Though there is an emphasis on most recent MCAT score, the admissions process also allows for consideration of the number of times the exam has been taken, timeline trends in MCAT scores, and highest sectional sub-scores to contextualize the holistic evaluation of an applicant.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo: Applicants who meet a minimum MCAT score of 498 and above will be considered.
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo: Applicants who meet a minimum BCPM GPA of 2.5 and above will be considered.  Applicants from disadvantaged backgrounds (especially those from Michigan) who would benefit from academic classroom enhancement in the sciences and are strong mission fits for our college are encouraged to apply and will be considered for matriculation to our Advanced Baccalaureate Learning Experience (ABLE) program.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: Applicants who meet a minimum BCPM GPA of 2.5 and above will be considered. Applicants from disadvantaged backgrounds (especially those from Michigan) who would benefit from academic classroom enhancement in the sciences and are strong mission fits for our college are encouraged to apply and will be considered for matriculation to our Advanced Baccalaureate Learning Experience (ABLE) program.
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: Aside from those selected for ABLE, applicants who would otherwise benefit from further academic enhancement to attain a competitive GPA are encouraged to do so.  Though there are no minimums in GPA or credits required, most successful applicants have completed at least 20 academic credits and a 3.5 GPA or higher in the area(s) needing enhancement; additional coursework in areas outside the academic need generally do not strengthen the application.  If/when possible, we encourage completion of a formal post-baccalaureate or graduate enhancement or career-changing program in order to optimize support and continued advising as it pertains to the entire application process.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: The College of Human Medicine accepts all coursework completed at a community college.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Letters of Intent, Interest, and notice of significant updates are only accepted from applicants placed on the alternate list.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo:
Candidates for an MD Degree must possess certain abilities and skills. MSU College of Human Medicine has established a set of technical standards necessary for medical students to achieve the knowledge, skills, and levels of competency for medical education and graduation. Students must attest to meeting the technical standards at the time of interview, matriculation, and on an annual basis thereafter.
Reasonable technical accommodation(s) can be made in some circumstances; however, the student must be able to perform in a reasonably independent manner with accommodation(s). If you believe you may need accommodation(s), please contact the MSU Resource Center for Persons with Disabilities.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: First semester in-state tuition + fees are $16,876 (out-of-state $30,788). Note: Tuition amounts reflect full-time attendance, and are for the 2025-2026 academic year. Tuition and fees subject to change by MSU Board of Trustees for the 2026-2027 academic year. It takes eleven semesters over four years to complete the degree. Information about financial aid can be obtained from the Office of Financial Aid at http://finaid.msu.edu/med or 517-353-2401.
medSchoolFinancial.tuitionPolicy: Tuition and fees are determined by the MSU Board of Trustees on an annual basis in approximately June for the following academic year.

medSchoolPrograms.info:
Advanced Baccalaureate Learning Experience (ABLE)  is a year-long enriched academic experience offered each application cycle to an invited group of disadvantaged students who have applied for admission to the College of Human Medicine.

Students who successfully complete the minimum requirements of the ABLE Program are offered regular admission to the entering College of Human Medicine class the following year. Individualized support in developing effective learning strategies as well as ABLE student activities combine to help promote academic success.

There is no direct application to the ABLE program. Selected disadvantaged applicants who show promise for medicine, yet may lack the science background required to perform optimally, are referred by the Admissions Committee to the ABLE Selection Committee following their interview for regular admission. The ABLE Selection Committee then makes the final selection for the ABLE program.

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: Based on continued mission-aligned review of alternates; not ranked.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec: Undergraduate coursework must be completed at an accredited US or Canadian four-year college or university. Community college courses are acceptable if the course(s) is accepted by an accredited four-year US or Canadian undergraduate institution as transfer credit. There is no requirement as to how recently your undergraduate courses or premedical requirements were completed; however, more recent coursework or advanced study in the basic sciences is preferred. There is no preference of where you complete your premedical courses, as long as they are completed at an accredited US or Canadian undergraduate institution.  Completion of a baccalaureate degree at an accredited United States or Canadian undergraduate institution is required.
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: No expiration date for previous coursework completed.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: The College of Human Medicine seeks a class that is academically competent, reflective of the rural and urban character of Michigan, and representative of a wide spectrum of personal characteristics, life experiences, and talents. Selection criteria are multi-factorial and include year-to-year and cumulative GPA (including post-bac and graduate); MCAT performance; fit with the school's mission; relevant clinical and community service; assessment of motivation; ability to communicate and problem solve; state of residence, and potential to contribute to the overall quality of the entering class. The college considers citizens of the United States and Canada.  Applicants with a US permanent resident visa (green card) or DACA (Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals) are also considered.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Long term, in-depth medical/clinical work and/or volunteer experiences will help a prospective applicant understand the medical profession while serving others. It is recommended to seek out medical, clinical, and shadowing opportunities, whether paid or volunteer.
